statement: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon with area 72. What is the area of the quadrilateral ACDF?

choices.misconception: I assumed the quadrilateral is exactly half of the hexagon.
I cut off only one corner triangle, ABC, and forgot the opposite one, DEF.
I gave the combined area of the two corner triangles that are cut off.
I thought each cut-off corner triangle was one eighth of the hexagon.

hints: What is left of the hexagon outside ACDF?
Split the hexagon into six equal equilateral triangles meeting at the centre. Compare one corner triangle such as ABC with those six pieces, then subtract.
With centre O, ABCO is made of two of the six triangles, and AC cuts it in half, so triangle ABC is one sixth of the hexagon.

solutions.reliable: Let O be the centre. The hexagon is six equal triangles of area 12. The rhombus ABCO is two of them, area 24, and the diagonal AC halves it, so triangle ABC has area 12. Likewise triangle DEF has area 12. So ACDF = 72 - 12 - 12 = 48. The transferable idea: cut a regular polygon into equal triangles from its centre, and areas of pieces become simple fractions.

whyOnTest: Dissection turns an awkward area into counting equal pieces, which is how most regular-polygon area questions are meant to be solved.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
